title: Deployment health gatekeeper with statistical change-point detection
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We need a statistically rigorous gate that prevents unhealthy model variants from progressing through canary or A/B rollouts. Current heuristics rely on fixed thresholds or single-metric alerts which either cause noisy interruptions or miss multi-signal degradations. Goal: Implement a Deployment Health Gatekeeper (DHG) that continuously scores a candidate variant using change-point detection and multi-signal fusion (latency, tail latency, error rate, token cost, throughput). The gate should support configurable sensitivity, hysteresis, and automated traffic quarantine actions, and integrate with Console dashboards and alerting. This ticket scopes the core detection, scoring, and action matrix plus integration tests and a staged rollout to internal services.
acceptance_criteria: DHG computes a per-variant health score every minute using at least 4 signals: p50 latency, p95 latency, error rate, and token cost
Change-point detector identifies sustained deviations vs a baseline window (configurable 30m-6h) with a false positive rate <= 2% on historical test traces

When score crosses configured strike threshold and persists for cooldown window, DHG triggers one of three automated actions: quarantine (0% new traffic), partial rollback (50% traffic shift), or rollout pause
Integration with Console: per-variant score, contributing signals, and recent change points visible on the model rollout dashboard
Automated tests and chaos experiments (latency injection, error spike, pricing impact) executed in staging with observed actions matching the playbook
proposal_summary: Build a statistical change-point based detector using a mixture of robust estimators (EWMA + CUSUM + bootstrap baseline) and a lightweight Bayesian changepoint check for low-traffic variants. Fuse signals into a single health score via logistic combination with tunable weights. Implement strike counts and cooldown windows (hysteresis) to avoid flapping. Actions are policy-driven and reversible; human-in-the-loop options available for P1 customers.
detection_algorithms: Baseline construction: rolling median + interquartile range (IQR) over configurable baseline window (default 2 hours)
Primary detector: CUSUM on z-scored metrics to detect persistent shifts in mean/level
Secondary detector for tails: robust EWMA on p95/p99 latency with long half-life to catch latency creep
Low-volume mode: Bayesian online change-point detection (Adams & MacKay) with prior tuned to avoid noisy signals
False-positive control: blocklist of maintenance windows and traffic anomalies; bootstrapped p-value estimation for each detected change point
scoring_and_thresholds: Health score range: 0..100 where lower is worse. Each metric maps to a subscore via sigmoid transform anchored at baseline +/- configurable deltas
Default weight vector: p95 latency 0.35, error rate 0.30, throughput 0.15, token cost 0.10, p50 latency 0.10 (tunable per-customer)
Strike policy: score < 40 increments a strike; three strikes within 15 minutes triggers automated quarantine unless manual override
Cost guardrail: if token cost increases > 30% and score drops to warning band, preferentially trigger cost-mitigation action rather than full quarantine
hysteresis_and_cooldown: Cooldown default: 10 minutes after any automated action during which DHG will not re-trigger an action for same variant unless severity increases
Backoff multiplier: each successive automated intervention within a 24h window doubles cooldown up to a 2h max to prevent oscillation
Recovery hysteresis: variant must hold score >= 70 for a sustained recovery window (default 30 minutes) before automated traffic ramp-up
Grace for transient spikes: single-minute blips are ignored unless supported by CUSUM persistence or bootstrapped p-value < 0.01
actions_and_playbook: No-op / warn: surface score + suggestion to on-call when score in warning band
Traffic quarantine: route 0% of new traffic to candidate and shift to previous stable variant with automatic fallbacks
Conservative rollback: reduce candidate traffic by configurable fraction (default 50%) and monitor for 30m
Pause rollout: stop automated ramp for all canaries in same model family and require manual resume
Manual override: support console button to force-advance or rollback with audit log; all automated actions create an incident ticket and post to rollout channel
testing_plan: Unit tests for signal transforms, scoring, and detector false-positive characteristics
Replay tests: run DHG on historical production traces (last 90 days) to validate FP rate and recall on known incidents
Chaos experiments in staging: inject latency tails, synthetic error bursts, and token-cost anomalies against a canary to validate action mapping
Shadow rollout test: run detector in dry-run mode for two weeks across internal services and collect operator feedback
KB docs + runbook to be reviewed by SRE, runtime, and product before GA
observability: Console dashboard: per-variant health score time-series, signal contributions, active strikes, and recent change points
Alerting: PagerDuty for P0/P1 actions; Slack summary for warnings; audit log export to BigQuery for post-mortem analysis
Metrics exported: detector_latency_ms, health_score, strikes_count, last_action, action_duration, baseline_window_size
Tracing: attach example traces for top contributing requests when a change point is detected
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager automated quarantines may cause availability regressions. Mitigation: Conservative defaults, strike counts, and staged ramp of automation per org tier
Risk: Low-volume variants produce noisy scores. Mitigation: Low-volume Bayesian detector and fallback to manual review for traffic < X rps
Risk: Signal correlation leads to double-counting (eg. throughput drops and latency increases). Mitigation: decorrelation step and principal-component regularization in scoring
Risk: Customer distrust of automated actions. Mitigation: audit trails, manual overrides, opt-in automation per customer tier
notes: Requested by product during Q1 reliability review; initial focus on hosted API then Dedicated customers
We should coordinate with legal for audit retention policy on automated actions for enterprise customers
Consider exposing a lightweight SDK so customers can run an offboarded DHG for private deployments if desired
